item.title: Upper Trapezius Pressure Release
clinicalUse: Localized myofascial tenderness reproducing familiar neck/shoulder symptoms
therapistPosition: Beside patient with good visual contact.
contact: Broad thumb/finger/knuckle contact over relevant muscle belly, away from anterior neck and nerve structures.
forceDirection: Gradual pressure into muscle until moderate tolerable discomfort, then hold rather than repeatedly poking.
safety: Stop with electric pain, paresthesia, dizziness or marked autonomic response.
item.visualCue: Gradual broad pressure → tolerable hold → slow release → movement re-test.

subTechniques.name: Upper Trapezius Trigger-Point Pressure Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce familiar local/referred pain and guarding when a clinically relevant trigger point is reproduced.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supported sitting or supine with the shoulder relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Use a broad thumb/finger pad or pincer-style contact over the taut/tender area without compressing the lateral neck.
subTechniques.direction: Increase pressure gradually until the patient's familiar discomfort is reproduced at a tolerable level; maintain without chasing severe pain.
subTechniques.dosage: 20–60 seconds, then release gradually. Reassess before repeating.
subTechniques.reassess: Local tenderness, cervical side-bending and the patient's familiar referred-pain pattern.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Familiar symptom reproduction is more meaningful than finding a random tender spot.
subTechniques.safetyNote: Avoid anterior neck pressure and stop with neurological or vascular-type symptoms.

subTechniques.name: Levator Scapulae Trigger-Point Pressure Release
subTechniques.clinicalGoal: Reduce medial-scapular/neck referral and improve comfortable rotation.
subTechniques.patientSetup: Supported sitting or side-lying with the arm and head relaxed.
subTechniques.contact: Broad sustained contact near the superior-medial scapular/levator muscle belly.
subTechniques.direction: Gradually increase to tolerable pressure and hold while monitoring the familiar symptom response.
subTechniques.reassess: Neck rotation, scapular tenderness and reaching.
subTechniques.clinicalPearl: Do not dig on the superior angle of the scapula; contact the muscle, not the bone.
